clue.text: Operatic MOT mechanics

parts.note: people who service vehicles for their annual MOT test are ..., and run together those two words name a Bizet opera

explanation.surface: A garage crew given to melodrama while testing cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles, so its mechanics are car men; 'Operatic' says to read them as one word naming an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera about the Seville cigarette girl is the work whose title the two words spell.

clue.text: Area in church where Monopoly card gets left

parts.note: Chance is one of the two card piles in the board game Monopoly

explanation.surface: A church area where someone leaves behind a Monopoly card.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Note to Frenchman, former German chancellor and artist

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
Willy Brandt was chancellor of West Germany

explanation.surface: A memo to a Frenchman, a German statesman and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Golden Age painter of The Night Watch.

clue.text: Crawler with hearing aid and false hair

parts.note: the ear is the organ that serves hearing
a wig is false hair

explanation.surface: A creep wearing a hearing aid and a toupee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' looks like a sycophant, but here it is a creeping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This pincered insect is a creeping creature, so a crawler; it also means a flatterer.

clue.text: Unending radiance and a melody about a Britten opera

indicators.note: unending says the word for radiance loses its final letter

parts.note: a glow is a soft radiance

indicators.note: about says the words for a melody are turned round

parts.note: a melody is an air, so 'a melody' gives AN AIR

explanation.surface: A glowing tune that wraps round one of Britten's stage works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but turns 'a melody' round; the opera's title is the old poetic name for Elizabeth I.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten wrote this opera for the coronation of Elizabeth II, taking the poetic name for Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Yobbo making fifty, getting dismissed

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A thug scores a half-century and is then out, as in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fifty runs is a milestone and a dismissed batsman is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbo is British slang for a loutish, uncouth young man.

clue.text: Delay execution of agent, always up about one

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent

indicators.note: about says the turned word wraps round the one
in a down clue, up says the word for always is read from the bottom

parts.note: ever means always
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Hold off putting a sales agent to death, always one to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns EVER into REVE, and 'about' puts I inside it, giving RIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a stay of execution is to postpone or cancel a punishment.

clue.text: Neil Armstrong, first to return from another world?

indicators.note: to return says the gathered letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written; the setter's route is the name plus a first letter, so the same letters reading backwards across 'Neil A' is a coincidence of that route, not a separate hiding

indicators.note: first says take the opening letter of Armstrong

explanation.surface: The first man on the Moon comes back from another world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reads NEIL plus A backwards, A LIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraterrestrial comes from a different planet; the question mark flags the playful link to the astronaut.

clue.text: Drivers pinching German car to tour island nation

indicators.note: pinching says the drivers' letters grip what follows

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: to tour says the car goes all round the island

parts.note: Merc is short for a Mercedes, a German car

explanation.surface: Motorists nick a German car to drive around an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this name, a nation in its own right.

clue.text: Strangely familiar if taken by Handel opera

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of familiar are jumbled, here with the letters of 'if' taken out of the pool

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Something oddly familiar, if Handel took it up as an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' signals that the letters of IF come out of FAMILIAR; 'Strangely' rearranges what remains, AMLIAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Handel's first opera, staged in Hamburg in 1705, bears this title.

clue.text: Heard knight got award for a Haydn symphony

indicators.note: heard says the phrase that follows is spoken and the entry is what it sounds like

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir, and an award is a prize, giving 'sir prize'

explanation.surface: A knight is honoured with an award for writing a Haydn symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's Symphony No 94 has a sudden loud chord in its slow movement, giving it its nickname.

clue.text: Monkey chewed end off fruit

indicators.note: chewed end off says the fruit loses its last letter

parts.note: the tamarind is a tropical fruit

explanation.surface: A monkey has bitten the end off a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American monkey related to the marmosets.

clue.text: Dvorak overture showing family vehicle in perpetual snow

parts.note: the family vehicle is the car
nival is a botanical adjective for things growing or living in perpetual snow

explanation.surface: A Dvorak overture played while the family car sits in endless snow.
explanation.walkthrough: NIVAL is a rare word, from Latin nix (snow), meaning living in or under snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvorak's concert overture of 1891 bears this festive title.

clue.text: Senior citizen with tattered notices removed for Wagner opera

indicators.note: tattered says the letters of the opening two words are torn up and rearranged, once the letters of 'notices' come out

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written: these letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: An old person with ragged posters taken down attends Wagner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' signals that the letters of NOTICES come out of SENIOR CITIZEN; 'tattered' rearranges the six left, EIRIZN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's early grand opera about the last of the Roman tribunes is named after its hero.

clue.text: Tough couple in Arkanas, America

parts.note: AR is the postal abbreviation for the US state Arkansas, misspelt in the clue
a duo is a couple

explanation.surface: A hardy pair living in Arkansas, USA.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue misspells Arkansas, whose postal code is AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult, laborious task is tough going.

clue.text: Nothing about unknown Mozart symphony

indicators.note: about says the word for nothing is turned round

parts.note: nil means nothing, as in a score
Z is one of the letters used in algebra for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A Mozart symphony nobody knows anything about.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's Symphony No 36 was written in the Austrian city and is named after it.

clue.text: Opera showing artist in Baltic land army

indicators.note: in says the artist goes inside the Baltic land

parts.note: Latvia is a Baltic state
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: An opera staged by a painter in a Baltic country's army.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera about the courtesan Violetta is titled 'the fallen woman'.

clue.text: Relief reduces, when eating cold sweets

indicators.note: eating says the word for relief takes the cold letter inside it

parts.note: aid is relief
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
drops means reduces

explanation.surface: Relief shrinks when someone eats cold confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: Acid drops are tart boiled sweets popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sharp-flavoured boiled sweets, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Is gender affecting his plans?

indicators.note: affecting says the preceding letters are worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is someone's gender influencing the plans they draw up?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a person who draws up plans, whose letters come from 'Is gender'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who draws up plans for clothes, buildings or products is the one the clue's question concerns.

clue.text: Father's article about quiet Beethoven piano sonata

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
'the' is the definite article

indicators.note: about here means in disorder, so the letters of quiet are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Dad's piece of writing on a quiet Beethoven sonata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram signal, turning QUIET into TIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No 8 in C minor is known by this French nickname meaning full of pathos.

clue.text: Country-lover is a soft touch about 3

indicators.note: about says the soft touch goes round the number

parts.note: a pat is a soft touch
a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: Someone who loves their country is easily gulled about the number three.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' looks like a cross-reference to 3 down, but it simply means a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to their homeland loves their country.

clue.text: An Indian, oddly, appearing in opera

indicators.note: oddly says take the odd-numbered letters of the words that come before it

explanation.surface: An Indian character turns up in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera about an Ethiopian princess enslaved in Egypt bears her name.

clue.text: Hunter who became a stag will perform for a long time

parts.note: to act is to perform
an aeon is a very long time

explanation.surface: A huntsman turned stag will act for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the hunter saw Artemis bathing, was turned into a stag and was killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: A bounder in iron in Entertainment by Walton

indicators.note: in says the 'A' and the bounder sit inside the iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a cad is a bounder

explanation.surface: A rogue inside an iron in a Walton entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: William Walton set Edith Sitwell's poems in this 'entertainment' of 1922.

clue.text: Heart-rending overture by Brahms at end of concert — smoke around!

indicators.note: at end of says take the final letter of the word concert
around says the word for a smoke is turned round

parts.note: a cigar is a smoke

explanation.surface: A moving Brahms overture closes a concert in a haze of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles up: the word means heart-rending, and Brahms wrote an overture of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahms wrote a Tragic Overture, and the word itself means heart-rending or calamitous.

clue.text: Everyone's entered for the wrestling match

definitions.meaning: with everybody inside, all the people are in
a freestyle wrestling bout with few rules is known by this term

explanation.surface: Everyone has signed up for the wrestling bout.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in wrestling is freestyle wrestling with almost no holds barred; the phrase also means everyone included.

clue.text: Poor tutor embracing joiner in Puccini opera

indicators.note: embracing says the shuffled tutor holds the joining word inside it
poor says the letters of tutor are in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
'and' is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: A hapless tutor hugs a carpenter during a Puccini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' looks like a carpenter but is the conjunction, a word that joins clauses.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's last, unfinished opera is named after its icy Chinese princess.

clue.text: Starts to study hard, exercising daily in the man's cave?

indicators.note: starts to says take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Begins hitting the books and working out every day in a man cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut is the classic man cave, a male retreat for hobbies and tinkering.

clue.text: Adult hotline may reveal Savoy operetta

indicators.note: may reveal suggests the letters, rearranged, can show something else

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sex chat line might expose a Gilbert and Sullivan piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy operas are Gilbert and Sullivan's, first staged at London's Savoy Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's fairy opera of 1882 was the first premiered at the Savoy Theatre.

clue.text: Transaction involves award for Richard Strauss opera

indicators.note: involves says the transaction wraps round the award

parts.note: a sale is a transaction
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A deal including a prize for a Strauss opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Strauss's one-act opera after Oscar Wilde's play centres on the biblical princess who demands John the Baptist's head.

clue.text: Ant and Dec start rehearsing one new Rossini opera

indicators.note: new says the gathered letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: start says take the opening letter of rehearsing

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: TV duo Ant and Dec begin practising a new Rossini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting duo.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini's opera of 1813 is named after its crusading knight hero.

clue.text: Admiral at Mass by Haydn in NZ city

definitions.meaning: the victor of Trafalgar is Britain's most famous admiral
Haydn's Missa in angustiis is nicknamed after the admiral
a city at the north of New Zealand's South Island

explanation.surface: An admiral attends a Haydn Mass in a New Zealand city.
explanation.definitionFit: One surname names the Trafalgar hero, the Mass Haydn wrote in 1798, and a South Island city.
